metadata.target_audience: Parents of school-aged children and teenagers (Ages 6–18)
metadata.core_objective: Shift from micromanaging homework to building sustainable study systems, self-advocacy skills, and academic ownership.

topics.title: From Homework Police to Academic Architect
topics.summary: Transferring ownership of school performance from parents to students through structured environments.
key_principles: Daily portal checking creates over-reliance and parental anxiety.
Architects build routines, launchpads, and time-boxing frameworks.

topics.title: Executive Functioning & Self-Advocacy
topics.summary: Building organizational habits and teaching students to communicate directly with educators.

activities.title: The Study Environment & Habit Audit
activities.instructions: Identify physical and organizational friction points in your home study routine.

activities.title: Scripting Student Self-Advocacy
activities.instructions: Practice coaching children to initiate academic conversations directly with teachers.

tasks.title: Academic Check-In Protocol Setup
tasks.action: Establish a weekly Sunday grade review time and pause daily portal surveillance.

quiz.question: What is the main problem with a parent constantly checking online grade portals multiple times a day?
options: A) It causes the school's online server to crash.
B) It shifts academic ownership and anxiety from the student to the parent, leading to nagging and reduced student self-reliance.
C) Teachers prefer parents to check grades every hour.
D) It makes the student study twice as fast.

quiz.question: How should a parent handle a middle-schooler who leaves their completed science project on the kitchen counter?
options: A) Drive it to school immediately and leave it at the main office with an excuse note.
B) Call the school principal to complain about homework policies.
C) Leave the project at home, allowing the student to experience the natural consequence and practice self-advocacy with the teacher.
D) Throw the project away to teach a lesson.
